title: Art Show
logline: Michael guest-lectures at Ryan's business school class and defends paper with his whole heart, then turns out to be the only person from the office at Pam's student art show, which Jim chose to miss.
outline: A: Michael lectures at Ryan's business school class, is wounded by Ryan's 'paper is dead' presentation, and humiliates him with sincerity; that night he's the only one who comes to Pam's art show, and he quietly rescues her painting. B: Pam's art show: Roy leaves early, Jim stays away on purpose, and the next day Pam tells him he should have come. C: Oscar notices Dwight and Angela have matching bobbleheads. Order: cold, B, A, C, A, B, A, B, C, A, B, tag
storySoFar: Michael guest-lectured at Ryan's business school class; Ryan presented 'Paper Is Dead', and Michael's sincere defense of paper got a standing ovation (Ryan got a B-minus). At Pam's student art show, Roy stayed two minutes, Oscar one, and Jim invented a client dinner to avoid watching Roy be her fiance; Michael came and stayed. Pam left her watercolor of the office building on the free table, and Michael secretly paid for it and hung it in his office; Pam doesn't know. She told Jim he should have been there. Oscar noticed Dwight and Angela's matching cat-sheriff bobbleheads. Earlier: Roy set the wedding for June 10; Jim confessed to Michael that he loves Pam and Michael is keeping it secret; Kelly kissed Ryan's cheek at bowling; corporate will close Scranton or Stamford; Jan says her kiss with Michael never happened.

stateChanges.progress: Jim skipped Pam's art show on purpose; she told him he should have been there
Michael's guest lecture humiliated Ryan with sincerity; Ryan got a B-minus
Oscar noticed their matching cat-sheriff bobbleheads

stateChanges.status: He was the only one at her art show; she hugged him

stateChanges.text: Michael secretly bought Pam's watercolor of the office building and hung it in his office; Pam thinks nobody took it
Jim lied about a client dinner in Carbondale to skip the art show

scenes.recap: A tiny radio hidden in the ceiling plays crickets; Dwight hunts for them all morning.

beats.text: Does anyone else hear crickets?
Crickets? In November?

beats.caption: climbs on his chair and pushes up a ceiling tile

beats.text: A cricket infestation can destroy a building in a week. I've seen it. In a barn.

beats.caption: turns a tiny dial under her desk; the crickets get louder

beats.text: THEY'RE BREEDING.

scenes.recap: Pam hands out flyers for her class's student art show on Thursday; Jim promises to come.

beats.text: So my class has a student show Thursday night. It's no big deal. There's cheese.
What kind of cheese?
I'll try to stop by. I love a student show. So much ambition.
Thursday. I'll be there. Front row. Do art shows have rows?

lines: I'm showing three pieces. Two still lifes and a watercolor of the building.
The office building. I know. It's what I see every day. It's kind of all I see.

scenes.recap: Ryan's professor wants a local manager to speak to the class; Ryan reluctantly asks Michael, who is overjoyed.

beats.text: My professor wants a local manager to speak to the class. About real-world business. Tomorrow.
Ryan. Are you asking me to be your teacher? Again? Officially?
The manager at Staples said no.
I accept. I'll bring handouts. And Dwight, for demonstrations.

lines: It's ten minutes. He'll talk about paper, everyone will be bored, and I'll get extra credit.

scenes.recap: Oscar notices Angela's new bobblehead is identical to one on Dwight's desk; both deny it.

beats.text: Angela, is that a bobblehead of a cat in a sheriff's hat?
It was a gift. From my sister.
Dwight has the exact same one. A cat. In a sheriff's hat.
Mine is a deputy. Completely different rank.

scenes.recap: Michael opens his guest lecture by calling Ryan 'like a son', then sits through Ryan's presentation, 'Paper Is Dead'.

beats.text: Good morning, future millionaires. I'm Michael Scott. Ryan is my temp. And, in a way, my son.
But first, Ryan has a presentation. Go, Ryan. Make me proud.
My presentation is called 'Paper Is Dead.' Companies like Dunder Mifflin will be obsolete in ten years.
Michael, say the word and I'll take him down.

scenes.recap: Jim tells Pam he can't make the art show because of a client dinner; his talking head tells the truth.

beats.text: Hey, so, Thursday. I've got a client dinner in Carbondale. I can't move it. I'm really sorry.
Oh. No, that's fine. Totally. It's just a student thing.
Show me everything Friday?
Sure.

lines: There's no client dinner. I just... can't stand in a room and watch Roy be her fiance right now.
She set a date. I need to get used to that. I'm getting used to it.

scenes.recap: Michael's rebuttal is a long, sincere defense of paper, which humiliates Ryan more than any insult could.

beats.text: Paper is dead? Paper is your birth certificate. Your diploma. Your first love letter.
When Ryan started, I gave him a stapler. I didn't email him a stapler. You can't email a stapler.
Ryan, I believe in you. You'll do great things. Just maybe not to my company.

beats.caption: someone in the back starts clapping

lines: The class gave Michael a standing ovation. I got a B-minus.
My professor wrote 'Your boss is right' on the rubric.

scenes.recap: At the art show, Roy looks for two minutes and leaves for the game; Oscar stops by politely and goes; Pam stands alone by her pictures.

beats.text: THURSDAY NIGHT
These are nice, babe. Real nice. The building one's good. Looks just like it.
Game starts at eight. I'll see you at home?
Pam, your lines are very confident. I mean that. I have to run. Book club.

beats.caption: Pam stands alone by her three pictures

scenes.recap: Angela demands Dwight hide his bobblehead; he hides it in his desk, but keeps it facing out.

beats.text: Oscar knows. You said nobody would notice two identical cat sheriffs.
Mine is a deputy, Angela.
Hide it.
I will hide it in my drawer. Facing out. So he can still see me.

lines: I don't have a sister. Don't tell anyone that either.

scenes.recap: Michael arrives, still glowing from his lecture, and loves her watercolor of the building; after she leaves it on the 'free' table, he quietly takes it and pays anyway.

beats.text: Pam! Am I late? I had a lecture. I'm a professor now. Kind of. Is this ours? Is this our building?
Yeah. You're the only one from work who came, actually.
Pam, this is... You made our building look like somewhere people would want to be.
Nobody's buying anything. I'm leaving the building one on the free table. It's too sad to carry home.

beats.caption: slips forty dollars into the class jar and takes the watercolor

lines: She can't know. She'd think it was weird. It is weird. But it's going on my wall.
And someday, when she's famous, I'll be rich. That's not why. That's partly why.

scenes.recap: Friday, Jim asks about the show; Pam tells him only Michael came, and that he should have been there.

beats.text: FRIDAY
So? How was it? Tell me everything.
Roy came for a minute. Oscar came for a minute. Michael came. Michael stayed.
Pam, I'm sorry. I should've been there.
Yeah. You should have.

scenes.recap: Michael hangs the watercolor in his office, crooked; Dwight asks what it is.

beats.caption: hangs a small watercolor of the office building, slightly crooked

beats.text: What is that?
Art, Dwight. Anonymous art. From an anonymous artist. Who I don't know.
It's our building.
Coincidence.
